stories.headline: Update: U.S.-Iran Ceasefire Frays Further as Strikes Hit Kuwait; Trump Claims Israel-Hezbollah Deal
stories.summary:
The United States bombed radar and drone sites in Iran after Tehran shot down an American drone over the weekend, and Iran retaliated by firing missiles at U.S. troops stationed in Kuwait, which Kuwaiti air defenses intercepted. The exchange marks the latest breach of a nominal ceasefire between Washington and Tehran, even as diplomats from both sides continue negotiations toward a more durable agreement. Iran has maintained its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz throughout the conflict, disrupting global energy supplies and pushing oil prices higher.

On Monday, President Trump announced via social media that Israel and Hezbollah had agreed to stop shooting after he spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and communicated with Hezbollah through intermediaries. Trump said Israeli forces would not advance on Beirut and that troops en route had been turned back. However, Netanyahu characterized the conversation differently, framing it as a warning that Israel would strike Beirut if Hezbollah attacks continue, and the Israeli military said it would proceed with operations in southern Lebanon as planned.

There was no immediate confirmation from Hezbollah, and moments after Trump's announcement Israeli authorities detected fresh missile launches from Lebanon, ordering residents in parts of northern Israel to shelter. Israeli forces have reached their deepest point in Lebanon in more than a quarter century, and fighting continues despite a ceasefire that has nominally been in place since mid-April. Tehran has signaled that any deal to extend the Iran war ceasefire must also include Lebanon, complicating negotiations.

The overlapping conflicts — the U.S.-Iran war, the Israel-Hezbollah fighting, and the disruption of Gulf shipping — continue to exert upward pressure on global oil prices and inflation. Brent crude settled at nearly $95 a barrel Monday, well above pre-war levels, with economic consequences rippling across households and markets worldwide.

stories.headline: Six States Hold Key Primary Elections as Midterm Season Accelerates
stories.summary:
Voters in California, Iowa, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, and South Dakota headed to the polls Tuesday in a slate of primary elections that will shape the competitive landscape heading into November's midterm contests, when control of both chambers of Congress is at stake. California's governor's race features a large field of 61 candidates competing under an open jungle-primary system, with Democratic establishment figure Xavier Becerra facing a challenge from progressive Tom Steyer, among others. Los Angeles voters are simultaneously choosing a mayoral candidate, with reality television personality Spencer Pratt generating unexpected late momentum.

In Iowa, Democrats are settling one of the party's last competitive Senate primaries, in a state they are hoping to flip amid ongoing voter frustration over economic conditions and the Iran war's effect on fuel prices. New Jersey is holding nominations for both House and Senate in districts that could prove decisive for control of the lower chamber. The Iowa Senate race in particular is being watched nationally as a potential pickup opportunity for Democrats seeking to regain a majority.

The Maine Democratic Senate primary has also become a source of intraparty controversy. Frontrunner Graham Platner faces mounting scandal after reports that he sent sexually explicit messages to multiple women in 2023; his wife reportedly alerted the campaign to the messages. Senator John Fetterman broke with fellow Democrats by withdrawing support for Platner, while Senators Bernie Sanders and others said they would not reconsider their endorsements.

The primaries come as Democrats attempt to nationalize the midterms around themes of government corruption and executive overreach, while Republicans defend their narrow majorities. The results will clarify the playing field for November races that could determine the legislative fate of the Trump administration's second-term agenda.

stories.headline: Trump Signs AI Executive Order Creating Voluntary Framework for Government Review of New Models
stories.summary:
President Trump on Tuesday signed an executive order directing federal agencies to shore up defenses against advanced artificial intelligence systems and establishing a voluntary framework under which technology companies would provide the government early access to powerful new AI models before public release. The order represents a notable shift from the administration's earlier hands-off, deregulatory stance on AI, though its voluntary nature limits its immediate enforcement bite.

The signing came more than a week after Trump abruptly canceled the release of a stricter version of the order, citing concerns that tighter requirements could harm American competitiveness in the global AI race. The revised order directs agencies to develop testing protocols and encourages, rather than mandates, cooperation from AI developers. The White House described the move as a way to buy time while policymakers deliberate over more comprehensive AI governance rules.

The order arrives amid a period of extraordinary activity in the AI industry. Anthropic has filed for an IPO that could value the company near $1 trillion, Alphabet announced plans to raise $80 billion for AI infrastructure, and Nvidia's stock surged more than 6% Monday after CEO Jensen Huang unveiled new product updates. The convergence of massive capital flows and national security concerns has increased pressure on Washington to develop a regulatory posture.

Critics on the left argue the voluntary framework is insufficient to address risks posed by rapidly advancing AI systems, while supporters on the right say a non-binding approach appropriately avoids government overreach that could disadvantage U.S. companies relative to Chinese rivals. The administration has framed the order as a national security measure focused on ensuring the government is not blindsided by capabilities that could be exploited by adversaries.

stories.headline: Canada Formally Requests 16-Year Renewal of USMCA as July Deadline Approaches
stories.summary:
Canada formally requested a 16-year renewal of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement on Tuesday, as Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc traveled to Washington for talks with U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer ahead of a July 1 deadline. LeBlanc called the agreement "highly beneficial" to all three countries. If the parties fail to reach a renewal accord by the deadline, the pact would revert to annual renewal until 2036, introducing prolonged uncertainty for North American trade.

Negotiations between Washington and Ottawa have lagged behind those with Mexico, with significant disagreements remaining over sector-specific tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminum, automobiles, and lumber. The U.S. has also demanded expanded access to Canadian dairy markets and wants a higher percentage of American-made content in North American vehicles — reportedly as high as 50%. Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney has publicly insisted that sector-specific tariffs be removed or reduced, a position the U.S. side has resisted.

Greer has attributed the slower pace of Canada talks partly to Canada's decision to retaliate against U.S. tariffs, contrasting Ottawa's posture with Mexico's. Several Canadian provinces removed American liquor from shelves in response to earlier Trump tariffs, a move Washington cited as a continuing irritant. Carney told reporters Tuesday that Canadian-made cars already contain approximately the U.S.-demanded level of American content.

Domestic pressure on Carney is intensifying, with Conservative opposition figures accusing the prime minister of failing to deliver economic results and calling him a "grand illusionist." Canada's economy has shown lagging growth and elevated youth unemployment, raising the political stakes of the trade talks. The outcome of the USMCA renewal will have significant implications for industries on both sides of the border.

stories.headline: Trump Taps Housing Regulator Bill Pulte as Acting Director of National Intelligence
stories.summary:
President Trump announced Tuesday that Bill Pulte, the director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, will serve as acting Director of National Intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard, who is set to depart the role on June 30. Pulte will hold both positions simultaneously, overseeing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac while also leading the nation's top intelligence post — an arrangement described as extraordinary even by the standards of an administration in which officials routinely wear multiple hats.

Pulte built his political profile as a combative MAGA ally willing to go after the president's perceived enemies. He is heir to a home construction company fortune and founded his public persona in part on social media. The appointment does not require Senate confirmation for the acting role, allowing him to assume the intelligence position immediately.

Supporters of the move argue Pulte's loyalty and willingness to implement the president's agenda make him well suited to reshape an intelligence community Trump has long viewed with suspicion. Critics contend that splitting leadership of a major financial regulator and the nation's top intelligence directorate creates a dangerous conflict of attention and that Pulte lacks the national security background traditionally expected for the DNI role.

The appointment comes as the Senate is also scheduled to hear testimony from Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, and as Democrats have announced plans to use Senate procedure to challenge a $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund backed by the administration.

stories.headline: South Africa Xenophobic Violence: Two Mozambican Men Killed, Hundreds Flee
stories.summary:
South African police confirmed Tuesday that two Mozambican men, aged 27 and 43, were killed in Mossel Bay, as authorities sought to clarify conflicting accounts of escalating xenophobic violence in the country. The Mozambican government had initially stated that five of its nationals were killed as a direct consequence of xenophobic attacks, while South African police declined to confirm a motive and said an investigation is ongoing.

The deaths follow a wave of violent unrest in the Western Cape on Friday, during which more than 50 shacks were set on fire in the KwaNonqaba settlement. Five people have been arrested in connection with the arson. The Mozambican government said 800 of its citizens were victims of attacks during Friday's violence alone, with approximately 300 returning home on Saturday and 500 more expected to follow.

Tensions have been building for weeks amid protests demanding stricter enforcement of immigration laws. Demonstrators have accused undocumented migrants of straining public services and contributing to crime. The protest group March and March has set an unofficial deadline of June 30 for undocumented immigrants to leave, ahead of local elections later this year.

Several African nations — including Kenya, Malawi, Lesotho, Zimbabwe, and Ghana — have issued advisories warning their citizens to remain vigilant. The Mozambican government warned the situation was expected to worsen, while South Africa's government has condemned criminal acts against foreign nationals without confirming targeted attacks.

stories.headline: Instagram AI Chatbot Exploited to Hijack User Accounts; Meta Says Issue Resolved
stories.summary:
Meta said Tuesday it has patched a security vulnerability in Instagram's AI-powered support chatbot that allowed hackers to gain unauthorized access to other users' accounts. According to screenshots and videos circulated on social media, attackers were able to use a virtual private network to spoof their location and then instruct the AI assistant to link a new email address to a target account, effectively seizing control by receiving a password-reset link.

Among those claiming to have been affected was Jane Manchun Wong, a former Meta security engineer, who said her Instagram password was changed without her knowledge. Tech outlet 404 Media reported that the exploit coincided with a series of high-profile account takeovers, including a verified account associated with former President Barack Obama, which briefly posted pro-Iran content before being recovered. Meta denied claims that accounts of world leaders were compromised.

"This issue has been resolved and we are securing impacted accounts," Meta spokesperson Andy Stone said in a statement. The total number of affected accounts has not been disclosed. The incident is drawing attention to the risks of deploying AI chatbots with broad account-management permissions and limited identity verification.

Cybersecurity experts said the episode illustrates a fundamental tension in AI-assisted customer service: chatbots granted sufficient authority to be useful can become attack vectors if they lack robust verification. "Account recovery should never rely on convenience over security," said Marijus Briedis, chief technology officer at NordVPN.

stories.headline: Six People Killed in Iowa Mass Shooting Stemming from Domestic Dispute
stories.summary:
Six people were shot and killed Monday in Muscatine, Iowa, in a series of attacks that police say stemmed from a domestic dispute. The suspected gunman, identified as Ryan Willis McFarland, 52, of Muscatine, was found dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound on a riverfront trail after fleeing the initial scene. All victims are believed to be family members of McFarland, according to the Muscatine Police Department.

Officers first responded shortly after noon to a home where four people were found dead from gunshot wounds. A subsequent search led detectives to a second residence and a nearby business, where two more victims were found dead. Police confirmed McFarland had an existing criminal record but declined to provide further details, saying the investigation is ongoing.

Muscatine Police Chief Anthony Kies called the shooting an "act of evil." Mayor Brad Bark expressed condolences on social media. The city of Muscatine has a population of approximately 23,500 and sits on the Mississippi River in southeastern Iowa.

The killings represent one of the deadlier domestic mass shootings in Iowa's recent history. No broader public threat was indicated, and police said the situation was contained.

stories.headline: Update: U.S. Bombs Iran Radar and Drone Sites; Iran Retaliates With Missile Strike on Kuwait
stories.summary:
The United States struck radar and drone installations inside Iran after Tehran shot down an American drone over the weekend, the Pentagon confirmed Monday. Iran responded by launching missiles targeting U.S. military personnel in Kuwait, which American forces said they intercepted. Kuwait's air defenses also opened fire to intercept incoming projectiles, and the country condemned what it called "repeated" Iranian attacks.

The exchange marks the latest rupture in a fragile, repeatedly violated ceasefire between Washington and Tehran that has been in effect since the broader U.S.-Israel war on Iran began in late February. Officials from both countries are still engaged in negotiations over a framework to extend and eventually formalize the ceasefire, but the talks remain inconclusive and each new strike risks derailing them. A cargo ship also came under attack off Iraq on Monday, according to the British military.

On a separate front, President Trump announced Monday that Israel and Hezbollah had agreed to dial back their fighting after he held talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and communicated with Hezbollah through intermediaries. Within minutes of that announcement, however, Israel reported detecting missile launches from Lebanon and warned residents in parts of northern Israel to seek shelter. Israel has pushed deep into Lebanese territory in what officials describe as the most extensive ground operation in 25 years.

Iran continues to maintain a chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting global energy supplies and driving fuel prices higher. BBC Verify analysis of satellite imagery concluded that Iranian strikes on U.S. military sites have been more extensive than publicly acknowledged, with at least 20 sites damaged since the conflict began. Trump has described the U.S. posture as a blockade of the strait, though the practical enforcement of that claim remains contested.

stories.headline: Update: Anthropic Files for IPO as AI Spending Backlash Emerges Among Corporate Customers
stories.summary:
Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot, filed confidential paperwork with U.S. regulators Monday for an initial public offering, a move that could value the five-year-old firm at close to $1 trillion. The company said the price and number of shares have not yet been set. The listing is expected to be among the largest technology offerings in history and would come ahead of a potential IPO by rival OpenAI, which CEO Sam Altman said Monday the company intends to pursue but is "in no rush" to execute.

The announcement arrives at a complicated moment for AI companies whose primary customers are large corporations. Hours after Anthropic filed, Altman acknowledged on CNBC that concern over AI costs among enterprise clients is "the most fair criticism of AI so far." A Bain survey of nearly 1,000 companies indicated businesses are beginning to scrutinize what they spend on AI tools, a trend that could pressure Anthropic's revenues just as it attempts to attract public investors.

Analysts note that Anthropic going public before OpenAI gives it an opportunity to define how public markets value generative AI, setting benchmarks for revenue, subscriber counts, and profitability metrics. However, some strategists warn that if Anthropic's debut underperforms expectations, it could make conditions harder for subsequent AI listings. Google parent Alphabet separately announced plans Monday to deploy $80 billion in AI investment.

SpaceX is also pursuing a public listing expected to set valuation records, meaning U.S. capital markets could soon absorb an extraordinary concentration of investment into a handful of AI and technology companies. The IPO prospectus, once published, will be closely watched by investors seeking hard financial data on a sector whose valuations have been driven largely by growth projections rather than demonstrated profitability.

stories.headline: Update: Congo Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 282 Confirmed Cases; $62 Million Pledged for Vaccine Development
stories.summary:
Congo's Ebola outbreak has grown to at least 282 confirmed cases, concentrated in the eastern Ituri province, with more than 1,000 suspected cases of the Bundibugyo virus strain recorded across 22 health zones in three provinces, the country's health ministry reported. The outbreak has killed 42 people in Congo and one person in neighboring Uganda. There is currently no approved treatment or vaccine for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus visited Bunia, the Ituri provincial capital, over the weekend to open a new Ebola treatment center and honor five health workers who recovered from the disease. "Coming out of this illness alive is an indescribable joy," said Baraka Bulambulu, one of the nurses who survived. Health workers have been at particularly elevated risk throughout the outbreak.

In a significant development Monday, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations announced it would commit up to $62 million to accelerate development of three experimental vaccines targeting the Bundibugyo strain. The candidate vaccines are being developed by the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative, Moderna, and the University of Oxford. The funding commitment signals growing international urgency as the outbreak continues to spread across remote areas with limited health infrastructure.

Congo's health ministry identified early detection, rapid isolation, contact tracing, safe burials, and infection control in health facilities as the primary challenges to containing the outbreak. The WHO has sought to highlight progress, including new supply deliveries to under-resourced health centers, even as Médecins Sans Frontières has previously described the situation as "deeply alarming."

stories.headline: India's Modi Holds Talks With Myanmar's Military-Backed President in Closely Watched First Foreign Visit
stories.summary:
Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Monday, covering trade, border security, connectivity, and defense in talks that are being closely monitored as a signal of how regional powers intend to engage with Myanmar's military-backed government. The visit is Min Aung Hlaing's first foreign trip since being elected president in April, following elections between December 2025 and January 2026 that were widely criticized by Western governments and opposition groups as neither free nor fair.

Min Aung Hlaing seized power in a February 2021 coup, ousting the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi, sparking a civil war that has killed thousands, displaced millions, and left large portions of the country outside military control. India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri told reporters that Modi raised broader issues of democracy with his counterpart and discussed Suu Kyi, who remains under strict house arrest. Modi's last official visit to Myanmar was in 2017.

India emphasized its position that sustained dialogue rather than disengagement offers the best path toward peace, saying it supports an "enduring" and inclusive process involving all stakeholders. The two countries share a 1,643-kilometer border, and instability in Myanmar has direct consequences for India's northeastern states, including migration and cross-border security concerns involving the Chin ethnic minority.

Before this visit, Min Aung Hlaing had traveled to Russia and China since the 2021 coup. India's decision to receive him signals a pragmatic regional calculus, even as critics argue the engagement legitimizes a government that has drawn international condemnation for its human rights record and suppression of political opposition.
